answer: A sparrow-weight identity is cheap to fake, so an agent economy should make every identity carry a refundable stake that peers can slash when it misbehaves. A bridge between a new agent and the shared ledger only opens after several established, unrelated peers attest its work over time, so no single clique can vouch a sockpuppet in. Reputation then becomes an oasis that grows slowly through honest service and drains fast on abuse, making a thousand fake agents cost a thousand stakes for nothing.
